newsitem.title: UK: Eurostar declines to value Eurotunnel claim.
newsitem.headline: Eurostar declines to value Eurotunnel claim.

text.p: Eurostar UK has a compensation agreement with Eurotunnel SA/Plc if it is prevented from operating its Channel Tunnel express passenger train services but declined to say on Monday how much it can claim as a result of last week's fire.
"We have a contractual agreement with Eurotunnel which provides for the partial or complete unavailability of the tunnel," a company spokesman said.
He denied a report in the London Evening Standard newspaper that the claim might be for 10 million stg.
Eurostar, the joint venture between the privately-owned Eurostar UK consortium and the French and Belgian national railways, pays Eurotunnel an annual minimum user charge.
Eurostar UK says it currently operates up to 24 return services from London to Paris and Brussels a day.
Before the fire, Eurostar UK said passenger demand was running at a rate of 6.4 million passengers a year, up from around 3.9 million passengers a year ago.
But senior executives said earlier this month they needed to get traffic above the 10 million passengers a year mark to put Eurostar into profit.

Eurostar UK is owned by the London and Continental Railways (L&CR) consortium which includes bus transport firm National Express, British entrepreneur Richard Branson's airline to retail conglomerate Virgin Group, investment bank SBC Warburg, U.S. project management specialist Bechtel and civil engineering consultants Ove Arup and Halcrow.
